$comment: Fleet executor registry, neutral defaults. Read with executors.md. Layers, later wins: this file, the user override {state_home}/executors.json (promotions write there), its projects.<repo> block, then <repo>/.plane/config.json fleet.executors. Objects merge key by key; lists and scalars replace.

claude.invocation: Agent tool: Agent(description, model, run_in_background: true, prompt: 'Invoke the <role skill> skill for <TICKET>. ...')
claude.notes: Today's behaviour and the fallback for every lane. Always pass an explicit model (`core/pm/skills/spawn.md` §3). Gated by the usage pacer hook.

codex.efforts_note: gpt-6-luna and gpt-5.6-luna stop at max. Omit --effort to use the config default (medium).

restricted.allows: workspace write, network, /tmp and the caches listed in the profile
restricted.blocks: every .git path (codex protects it even when granted write). No commit, no branch, no worktree add.
restricted.use_for: roles that edit files but never commit (none today)

full.use_for: engineer and tester: both commit and push

codex.quota: ChatGPT plan quota, separate from Claude. Not seen by the usage pacer.
codex.notes: Opt-in. Needs the codex CLI and the two profile files from core/references/codex-profiles/. Add codex candidates in your user override.

opencode.install: npm i -g opencode-ai (official package, GitHub latest release)
opencode.key_source: env_names from the environment, else env_file when the user override sets one. Values never reach argv, logs or stdout.
opencode.models_source: GET https://ollama.com/v1/models with the key, 2026-10-16 (20 models). opencode's built-in catalog also lists older ids that the API no longer returns; trust this list.

read-only.note: no --auto: plan's ask-gated edit/bash stay denied

write.note: auto-approves permissions; no OS sandbox. Not used for any role yet.

opencode.quota: Ollama Cloud plan quota, separate from Claude. Not seen by the usage pacer.

config_content.$comment: Passed per run as OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT. A headless opencode run auto-rejects reads outside the working dir, and one rejection ends the run. The role skills live in the fleet folder, so allow exactly that. opencode applies the LAST matching pattern, so the catch-all deny comes first.

opencode.notes: Opt-in. Needs the opencode CLI and an ollama-cloud provider in its config (see executors.md).
opencode.default_model_why: A code-specialised model built for tool use; a read-only scan is mostly file reads and greps.

providers.$comment: A model id without a provider/ prefix uses `provider` above. Pass provider/model for the others.
providers.ollama-cloud: Ollama Cloud plan (OLLAMA_API_KEY). Same plan as the claude-ollama executor.
providers.opencode: opencode's own hosted models. The *-free ones cost nothing and need no key; free tiers may keep prompts.
providers.zai-coding-plan: Z.ai GLM coding plan, through `opencode auth login`.

opencode.free_models_source: `opencode models`, 2026-10-22. Only a fallback when no discovery ran in free_model_policy.max_age_days: free models change almost daily, so `fleet free-models refresh` finds today's (freemodels.py). Two of these six were gone by 2026-10-25.
opencode.efforts: Passed as --variant <effort>. Names are the provider's own (e.g. minimal, high, max); an unknown one is the provider's error.

claude-ollama.provider_note: Ollama Cloud speaks the Anthropic Messages API at https://ollama.com/v1/messages, so Claude Code runs on it unchanged. The runner sets ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN for the child only and maps every model alias (opus, sonnet, haiku, subagents) to the lane's model, so nothing in the lane reaches Anthropic.
claude-ollama.models_source: GET https://ollama.com/v1/models with the key, 2026-10-16 (20 models). opencode's built-in catalog also lists older ids that the API no longer returns; trust this list.
claude-ollama.default_model_why: Only what `fleet models` prints. No role uses this executor unless a candidates list names it.

full.use_for: engineer and tester: both commit and push

read-only.note: Tested 2026-10-16: plan mode blocks MCP calls even with an allow rule, so read-only is a tool list instead. Edit tools are denied; Bash is allowed and is not sandboxed, like opencode's plan agent. The brief forbids writes and Plane changes.

claude-ollama.mcp_note: The lane loads only these MCP servers (--strict-mcp-config), copied from mcp_source into a 0600 file in the lane's out dir and deleted when the lane ends.
claude-ollama.quota: Ollama Cloud plan quota, the same plan opencode uses. Separate from Claude. Not seen by the usage pacer.
claude-ollama.notes: Opt-in. Same harness, skills, hooks and CLAUDE.md as a Claude lane, with an open model behind it. Not in any candidates list by default.

antigravity.install: Antigravity CLI (agy), signed in with the Google account that holds the AI Pro plan
antigravity.models_source: `agy models`, 2026-10-26. It lists each model per effort (gemini-3.8-flash-high, ...); the runner passes the base id and --effort, which agy accepts.
antigravity.efforts_note: agy --effort takes low|medium|high|xhigh|max, but `agy models` lists only low, medium and high (gpt-oss-120b: medium only).

full.use_for: engineer and tester: both commit and push

read-only.note: Same flag as full: the lane guard hook is the gate. Measured 2026-10-26 on agy 1.3.1: a hook can deny but cannot grant (allow, ask and permissionOverrides never passed agy's own check headless), and agy's own denial ends the run with no report, while a hook denial reaches the model and the run goes on. So agy allows everything and the guard denies writes, unlisted commands, Plane writes and any tool outside read_tools.

lane_guard.$comment: Policy for core/references/antigravity-plugin/lane-guard.mjs, a PreToolUse and Stop hook that acts only in fleet lanes (run-lane sets FLEET_LANE_POLICY). agy has no per-run tool list, so this is how a lane loses browser tools and how a read-only lane gets its commands without global allow rules.

antigravity.mcp_note: agy reads MCP servers only from ~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json (no per-run flag). `fleet antigravity-setup` registers each server there as `fleet mcp-exec <name>`, which reads the real entry from mcp_source at start. No secret is copied. The lane guard turns off every other MCP server in a lane.
antigravity.quota: Google AI Pro plan, separate from Claude. Three pools with their own windows, read live by `agy -p /usage` (see budget.executors.antigravity).
antigravity.notes: Opt-in. Claude models here run on the Google plan, not on the Claude subscription. Global agy plugins still load in every lane; the lane guard denies their tools.

scan.note: read-only scans: triage, counting, log reading, summaries. No role skill; the brief is the whole task.

pm.note: The PM is the Claude session itself. Never a lane.

escalation.$comment: If any trigger fires for a role, use this instead of the role default. Name the trigger in the pick line.

fallback_rules.registry_missing: use claude with the PM's model defaults
fallback_rules.lane_failed: non-zero exit, status != completed, no PR for an engineer, or timeout -> dead session (`core/pm/skills/spawn.md` §3 heartbeat), then re-queue once on the role's fallback
fallback_rules.budget: selection skips executors whose budget is hold or stop; pinned roles wait for resume_at

api.hint: server endpoints, services, DTOs, guards; no schema change

ui.hint: client components, templates, styling, client data access

money-concurrency.hint: money movement, balances, locks, ordering, timing

copy-i18n.hint: labels, translations, static text only; no logic, data or permission change

tests-only.hint: adds or fixes tests, no product code

retest.hint: a tester re-checking a reworked PR

rework.hint: a second engineer attempt after Rework

selection.no_explore: urgent or trunk-red fixes, kinds with allow_explore=false, any second attempt after Rework, and the tester of an experimental engineer
selection.$comment: Portable work moves to another candidate when its champion has no budget. Pinned work (testers, escalations) waits.

candidates.$comment: Per role, per task kind ('*' = any kind without its own list). First is the champion, the rest are challengers. Claude only by default; add codex/opencode entries in your user override to opt in.

families.$comment: An '<executor>:<prefix>' or '*:<prefix>' key matches models that start with <prefix>; '*:' covers every executor that serves open models (opencode, claude-ollama).

cost_weights.$comment: Relative cost units per million tokens, only to compare candidates. Tune freely. Keys: executor:model, then executor:provider/ (opencode models named provider/model), then executor.

free_model_policy.$comment: Free models may keep prompts. `free-models refresh` keeps the opencode models that cost nothing, call tools and have min_context; pick adds the live ones as challengers for `roles` only, drops them from every other role, and run-lane refuses them elsewhere or outside a read-only sandbox. Owner decision 2026-10-25: read-only scans only.

prices.$comment: USD per 1M tokens, for `cost` only: API list prices to compare options. Plans (Claude Max, ChatGPT, Ollama Cloud) bill differently. A model id matches its exact key, else the longest key it starts with. cache_read defaults to 0.1 x input when absent. Add other executors' models in the user override; a model with no price shows tokens only, never a guessed dollar figure.

claude-haiku-5-5.$comment: cache_read not published in the source; 0.1 x input assumed

budget.$comment: Same shape for every executor. Override per user in {state_home}/budget.json. Switch files in {state_home}: pacer-off / pace-off (all executors) or pacer-off-<executor> / pace-off-<executor>. pace-off skips the pace rule and keeps the hard stop.

claude.$comment: status_file: a file a statusline relay writes with the harness's rate_limits block. None = no meter, no judgement.

claude-ollama.$comment: state_as: shares the lane counter and any 429 back-off with opencode, since both draw on one Ollama Cloud plan.

pools.$comment: Model id prefix -> the /usage bucket ids it draws on; the longest prefix wins. From `agy -p /usage --output-format json`, 2026-10-26, Pro plan: Argon has its own weekly limit there.

antigravity.$comment: A live meter. Each lane is judged on its model's pool, every window in it (5h and weekly). The reading is cached cache_minutes, since the call takes about 4 s.
